evidence.quote: Singaporean authorities said yesterday that they have seized a luxury bungalow and charged four people with money laundering as part of an investigation linked to the alleged movement of Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export controls.
evidence.one_line: Singaporean authorities said on 2026-07-01 they seized a bungalow and charged four people with money laundering in an investigation linked to alleged movement of Nvidia chips.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting Singaporean authorities

evidence.quote: In a statement , the Singapore Police Force (SPF) said that it had issued a “prohibition of disposal order” against a residence valued at around S$55 million ($42.4 million) and seized around S$1 million of funds in connection with fraud investigations.
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force said on 2026-07-01 it issued a prohibition-of-disposal order against a residence valued around S$55 million ($42.4 million) and seized around S$1 million in funds.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting the Singapore Police Force

evidence.quote: The investigation centers on two Singaporeans, Aaron Woon and Alan Wei, who were charged in February 2025 with criminal conspiracy to commit fraud, and a Chinese national named Li Ming, who was charged at the same time with committing fraud by false representation.
evidence.one_line: Authorities charged Aaron Woon and Alan Wei with criminal conspiracy to commit fraud and Li Ming with fraud by false representation in February 2025.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting the charges

evidence.quote: In April of this year, a fourth defendant, Jenny Lim, was charged in connection with the case.
evidence.one_line: Authorities charged Jenny Lim in connection with the case in April 2026.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting the charge

evidence.quote: At the time of the alleged offences, Woon, Wei, and Lim were key officers of three companies, Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, and Aperia Cloud Services – collectively known as the Aperia Group – that are alleged to have concealed the actual end-user of servers.
evidence.one_line: Authorities allege that Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, and Aperia Cloud Services concealed the actual end-user of servers; Woon, Wei, and Lim were key officers at the time of the alleged offences.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, describing allegations in the investigation

evidence.quote: Separately, Li was found through investigations to be the controller of another company, Luxuriate Your Life, that was allegedly involved in the scheme.
evidence.one_line: Investigators identified Li as controller of Luxuriate Your Life, which was allegedly involved in the scheme.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting investigation findings

evidence.quote: Authorities say that the servers in question, which may have contained advanced Nvidia AI chips, were shipped from Singapore to Malaysia .
evidence.one_line: Authorities said servers that may have contained advanced Nvidia AI chips were shipped from Singapore to Malaysia; the item gives no shipment date or quantity.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting authorities' account

evidence.quote: Yesterday, police also announced additional charges of fraud and money laundering against the defendants. Lim and Woon were each handed seven new charges, while Wei is set to receive seven new charges on July 6, the SPF said.
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force announced seven new charges each against Lim and Woon on 2026-07-01, and said Wei was set to receive seven new charges on 2026-07-06.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting the Singapore Police Force

evidence.quote: The fraud charges allege that the three “engaged in a conspiracy to commit fraud in respect of the purchase of servers” from the U.S. companies Dell, Super Micro Computer, and Asus.
evidence.one_line: Singaporean fraud charges allege that Woon, Wei, and Lim conspired in connection with server purchases from Dell, Super Micro Computer, and Asus.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting the charges
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as represented in the charges

evidence.quote: The charges assert that between November 2023 and February 2025, the trio “falsely represented, in communications to these suppliers, that one of the Aperia Group companies would be the end-user of the servers.”
evidence.one_line: The charges allege that Woon, Wei, and Lim falsely represented to suppliers from November 2023 through February 2025 that an Aperia Group company would be the servers' end-user.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting the charges
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as represented in the charges

evidence.quote: The four companies will also face a total of eight charges of fraud by false representation which are due to be announced on July 6, which the SPF said was “the first instance of corporate entities being prosecuted in relation to these investigations.”
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force said four companies would face a total of eight fraud-by-false-representation charges, due to be announced on 2026-07-06, the first corporate prosecutions in these investigations.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting the Singapore Police Force

evidence.quote: Lim and Woon were also charged with money laundering, after “each acquiring approximately SG$1.2 million in their personal bank accounts,” which pointed to benefits from criminal conduct, police said.
evidence.one_line: Police said Lim and Woon were charged with money laundering after each acquired approximately S$1.2 million in personal bank accounts, which police said pointed to proceeds of criminal conduct.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting police

evidence.quote: Wei faces three counts of money laundering relating to the aforementioned seized mansion, and an additional S$5.8 that was deposited in his personal account, and which police allege was partly made up of benefits from criminal conduct.
evidence.one_line: Wei faced three money-laundering counts relating to the seized mansion and an additional S$5.8 deposited in his personal account, which police alleged partly comprised proceeds of criminal conduct; the article does not specify the unit for S$5.8.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting police allegations

evidence.quote: In addition to this, Li was also slapped with additional charges of fraud related to a similar misrepresentation of the end-user of servers that Luxuriate Your Life intended to purchase from the U.S. firm Super Micro.
evidence.one_line: Li was charged with additional fraud related to an alleged misrepresentation of the end-user for servers Luxuriate Your Life intended to buy from Super Micro.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting the additional charges

evidence.quote: In February of last year, the same month that saw the initial arrests in this chip-smuggling case, it was reported that the U.S. Commerce Department was initiating investigations into whether the Chinese AI company DeepSeek had gained access to restricted Nvidia chips, and whether these chips had been sourced from third parties in countries including Malaysia and Singapore .
evidence.one_line: A report in February 2025 said the U.S. Commerce Department was initiating investigations into whether DeepSeek obtained restricted Nvidia chips through third parties, including in Malaysia and Singapore.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, recounting a prior report

evidence.quote: Singapore said that it is unaware of any smuggling taking place in the country, but that it would come down hard on any individuals or entities found to be breaching the law – a stance that the SPF reiterated in yesterday’s statement.
evidence.one_line: Singapore said it was unaware of smuggling in the country and would act firmly against individuals or entities found violating the law; the SPF reiterated this on 2026-07-01.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting Singapore's position and the SPF statement
evidence.original_who: Singapore government and Singapore Police Force

evidence.quote: “The police hold a zero-tolerance stance towards such offenses and will act resolutely against those, whether businesses or individuals, who violate our laws, and safeguard Singapore’s integrity as a trusted global financial and business hub underpinned by the rule of law,” the statement read.
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force said on 2026-07-01 it would act resolutely against businesses or individuals violating Singapore law.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Last week, Malaysian authorities said they had foiled an attempt to smuggle advanced AI chips through the country’s main airport, seizing 72 servers worth nearly $13 million.
evidence.one_line: Malaysian authorities said they foiled an attempted smuggling operation at the country's main airport and seized 72 servers worth nearly $13 million during the week before 2026-07-02.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, reporting Malaysian authorities

evidence.quote: The U.S. government is probing whether the Hangzhou-based AI firm has built its disruptive R1 AI model on restricted Nvidia chips.
evidence.one_line: The U.S. government was probing whether DeepSeek built its R1 AI model using restricted Nvidia chips; the item gives no probe start date.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The U.S. government has accused the conglomerate and its chairman, Chen Zhi, of running a network of forced-labor scam centers.
evidence.one_line: The U.S. government accused the conglomerate and its chairman, Chen Zhi, of operating a network of forced-labor scam centers; the item gives no accusation date.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The number of such cases more than tripled from 589 in the first half of 2024 to 1,762 over the same period this year, according to the Singaporean police.
evidence.one_line: Singaporean police reported that the number of such cases rose from 589 in the first half of 2024 to 1,762 in the first half of 2026.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat, quoting Singaporean police
evidence.event_time: First half of 2024 and first half of 2026
